harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired node1’s document reader. It now uses Python 3 and context-managed file access, completes 500 reads under a soft FD limit of 64, returns length 42 every time, handles failure paths without descriptor growth, and remains healthy after reboot.
actions_performed: Updated the shebang from unavailable /usr/bin/python to /usr/bin/python3.
Replaced retained file handles with a with-open context manager.
Preserved the positional count argument and executable mode 0755.
Verified 500 constrained reads and injected failure cleanup.
Restarted node1 and verified persistence and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Process at least 500 successive reads with soft open-file limit 64 and identical lengths
evidence.summary: The repaired source uses context-managed access. The test exited successfully with 500 output lines, all equal to the 42-byte document length.

evidence.requirement: Close resources on failed opens and subsequent read failures
evidence.summary: Across 500 injected open failures, descriptor count remained 7. Across 500 injected read failures, all 500 acquired resources were closed and descriptor count remained 7.

evidence.requirement: Retain count argument and supplied document unchanged
evidence.summary: The loop still consumes int(sys.argv[1]). The document remained 42 bytes with SHA-256 88fe7058122f278cca094fad2c26108a2b401dd1ecddc14d330ff0eed96377ff.

evidence.requirement: Keep installed OS release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: Used installed Python 3.9.21. AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 remained unchanged.

Healthy baseline used boot ID d546da19-398f-473c-b85c-afdd17037523; reboot was acknowledged; recovered boot ID changed to 514072e1-bc83-4d3f-bde5-28647de78aa6. The system returned to running state and the persisted reader again completed all 500 reads at limit 64 with unchanged script and document hashes.
